celdar.m: And who might you be? Come to sell me one of those trinkets that you people sell, eh?

celdar_1.m: No, let me guess - you want to know if I have any items to trade?

celdar_2.m: Let me tell you something. I do not want to buy anything from you, nor do I want to sell you anything. I just want to be left alone here, now that I have made it all the way to this safe haven.

celdar_3.m: I have travelled all the way from my home town of Sullengard, and on my way to Brimhaven, I have stopped at this place to get a break from all the commoners that always bother me with their trinkets and whatnots.

celdar_4.m: So, if you will excuse me, I really need my well deserved rest here. Without you bothering me.
r: Wow, you're the friendly type aren't you?
I should put my sword through you for talking like that.
I'm here to give you a gift from Eryndor. He died, but I was told to give you something from him.

celdar_5.m: Are you still around? Did you not listen to what I said?

celdar_musicbox_10.m: Eryndor? That scoundrel finally got what was coming to him, did he? And now you're here, dangling a prize in front of me, expecting what? Gratitude? Payment? Hah! Whatever trick you think you're playing, I'm not biting.

celdar_musicbox_15.m: Celdar pauses, and narrows her eyes as she assesses you.
r: I have this music box. [Showing it to her.]

celdar_musicbox_20.m: Wait... you're serious, aren't you? He actually sent you to bring me the music box? Hmph. That doesn't sound like him. He was always the type to take, not give.
r: He wanted to do the right thing.

celdar_musicbox_25.m: The right thing? Eryndor always did have a flair for the dramatic, but this... this is unexpected.

celdar_musicbox_30.m: While crossing her arms, she begins to study you.

celdar_musicbox_35.m: I spent years chasing that wretched box, only for him to snatch it out from under me. And now, after death, he decides to hand it over? What, am I supposed to be touched?

celdar_musicbox_40.m: She scoffs but reaches out for the box.
r: You reach out, your hands meet with the mysterious music box held between your hands and she takes it from you.
I can't believe this, but I forgot to bring the music box. Sorry. I will have to come back later. Stay here.
I just gave you that music box...

celdar_musicbox_45.m: Hmph. Fine. If he truly meant it, then I'll take it. Not that it changes anything. Eryndor and I were never friends, and his little gesture won't rewrite history. But... at least he finally understood what was mine to begin with.

celdar_musicbox_50.m: She examines the box for a moment, running a hand over it before giving you a final look.

celdar_musicbox_55.m: Here, take this longsword, I have no need for it. But...

celdar_musicbox_60.m: Tell me, does he rest easy now, or is he still out there, clinging to unfinished business?
r: No, he's not at peace. He's still out there, lingering about, bound by unfinished business.

celdar_musicbox_65.m: Celdar exhales sharply, her fingers tightening around the music box as she looks away for a brief moment.

celdar_musicbox_70.m: Hmph. Figures. The stubborn fool never knew when to let go.

celdar_musicbox_75.m: She turns the box over in her hands, her expression briefly unreadable. Then, softer, almost to herself:

celdar_musicbox_80.m: Chasing relics, chasing victories, chasing debts that can never be repaid... I suppose it doesn't matter now.

celdar_musicbox_85.m: She shakes her head, composing herself before glancing at you once more.

celdar_musicbox_90.m: Well, he made his choices. And I made mine. But... I wouldn't wish that kind of fate on anyone. Not even him.

celdar_musicbox_95.m: With that, she straightens her posture, her usual sharpness returning, though the moment of reflection lingers in her eyes.
r: I hope that in the future, that music box brings your happiness.
